source.title: Turn user feedback into reviewed goals and iterative delivery
source.body:
## Feedback
> When I add issues that is my feedback the loop must handle it and ensure it gets broken down and planned and persisted as feedback and anchored into widened rules and deliverable goals that we can iterate on.

## Goal
A collaborator can submit an ordinary Issue. The loop owns clarification from existing context, planning, delivery and verification; the user supplies direction and consequential product decisions only.

## Required cycle
1. Preserve the original feedback and its revisions on the Issue. Respect explicit report-only instructions.
2. Inspect current behavior and existing work. Derive a measurable goal and the smallest useful next deliverables without duplicate owners.
3. Widen existing rules from observed cases; anchor subjective language in named observers and pass conditions. Keep acceptance in scenario/design specifications, with independent review of changes.
4. Publish native child Issues and blocked-by dependencies. GitHub Issues are the canonical work orders, including priority, scope, progress and delivery links.
5. Build, review, repair and land each bounded deliverable. Use evidence to compare the new behavior with the original goal.
6. A fresh verifier either records goal completion or opens the next bounded iteration. Merged children or green tests alone do not close the feedback Issue.

## Failure cases
- No duplicate work when a matching Issue, PR or live Claim exists.
- Bot progress updates do not retrigger planning; changed human feedback or delivered work does.
- Report-only feedback is preserved without implementation intake.
- Dependency/API failures remain visible and owned by engineering.
- New or cancelled dependencies cannot be treated as completed work.

## In progress
The initial migration has imported 31 unfinished Work rows into Issues and native dependencies. Queue/controller changes are being implemented on `codex/issue-work-orders`. Feedback planning and independent goal verification remain to be delivered; this Issue does not claim they already exist.

goals.statement: A new or substantively edited Issue from a repository owner or collaborator starts feedback planning with no scheduling label added by the user. The original human text and its revisions stay on the source Issue. Bot progress edits, `loop:status`, `loop:work` scheduling changes and an explicit `loop:report-only` instruction start no planning or implementation.
goals.observer: On current main, `python3 loop/feedback.test.py` passes l90_collaborator_feedback, l90_untrusted_author, l90_report_only, l90_bot_update and l90_changed_human_feedback. On GitHub, #394's feedback Claim records the source revision of the human text, and the feedback.yml run for #394 was dispatched by reconcile, not by a user-applied label. Passes when all of these hold.

goals.statement: A fresh planner inspects current behavior and existing Issues, PRs and Claims, then derives an observable goal and one bounded next batch of at most four deliveries. Each delivery reuses a matching owner instead of duplicating it, and each has an owner scope, an acceptance observer, regressions and real blocked-by dependencies.
goals.observer: The planning PR for #394 at its exact head lists at most four deliveries. Every delivery whose Key or scope matches an existing work Issue reuses that Issue's number, title, body and dependencies unchanged. No new loop:work Issue duplicates an existing Key: `gh issue list --label loop:work --state all` shows each Key once. Passes when all of these hold.

goals.statement: When a case exposes missing rule coverage, the rule is widened and anchored, keeping its examples and counterexamples. Acceptance stays in scenario and design files. The plan and any rule change pass an independent exact-head review before any child implementation is authorized.
goals.observer: #394's planning PR has an approving `VERDICT:` from a reviewer run other than the planner, on the PR's exact head. No child of #394 received `ready-for-agent` from the feedback controller before that approval: compare label event timestamps with the verdict timestamp. Any proposed rule appears as a scenario-file change in the same reviewed PR. Passes when all of these hold.

goals.statement: The trusted controller publishes approved deliveries as native GitHub child Issues with native blocked-by dependencies. Issues hold priority, scope, progress and delivery links. A new, open or cancelled dependency never counts as completed work.
goals.observer: `gh api repos/saadshahd/roundup/issues/394/sub_issues`, or #394's blocked-by list for owners that already have another parent, lists every approved delivery. Each child's `dependencies/blocked_by` matches its approved `blocked_by`. Each child body carries `Key:`, `Priority:` and `Mode:`. `loop/rules.sh ready --json` does not offer a child whose dependency is open or closed as not_planned. l90_cancelled_dependency passes. Passes when all of these hold.

goals.statement: Each bounded delivery is built, reviewed, repaired if needed and merged through a PR that names its Issue. Evidence compares the new behavior with the original goal.
goals.observer: For every child of #394, a merged PR names the child with `Refs #<n>` or `Closes #<n>`. The PR has an approving exact-head `VERDICT:` and passed check, rules and merge-ready. The child closed as completed only when its own acceptance observer was demonstrated. Passes when this holds for every child.

goals.statement: A fresh verifier observes every goal on current main, keeps the command output and run or capture links, and either records that each goal is complete or opens the next bounded iteration. #394 closes only after independently reviewed goal evidence, never from merged children, matching test names, bot comments or green CI alone.
goals.observer: A feedback.yml verify run for #394 on a main that contains every delivered child records each goal's index, command, output and HTTPS run URL. #394 is closed only by the trusted controller, after an independent review approves that verification at its exact head. Otherwise the verify proposal names open successor work. l90_independent_goal_verification and l90_unreviewed_or_stale_closure pass. Passes when all of these hold.

goals.statement: Dependency and API failures in feedback intake, planning, publication or verification stay visible and owned by engineering. They are never silently treated as success, and they never become a question for the user.
goals.observer: On current main, l90_bad_input_stops_before_network, l90_spend_timeout_leaves_no_claim_or_dispatch and l90_lost_issue_response_reuses_the_created_child pass. A failed feedback.yml run appears as a failed run, not a skipped one, and a failed feedback run left no `needs-you` comment on its source Issue. Passes when all of these hold.

deliveries.title: L90: turn feedback into reviewed plans and independently verified goals
deliveries.body:
## Outcome
Make collaborator feedback automatically reach a reviewed plan, bounded deliveries and independent goal verification. Preserve source feedback in Issues and iterate from observed results.

## Acceptance
Scenarios: L90
Specification: [scenarios/loop-rules.md](https://github.com/saadshahd/roundup/blob/main/scenarios/loop-rules.md)

## Scope
`loop/`, the smallest feedback workflow/prompt and vendored widen/anchor skills, and coordinated review gates for planning PRs. Reuse the shared Claims, build/review/repair controllers and canonical Issue format. Do not create a second file-based work queue.

## Preserve
L23/L24/L34/L46/L80/L87/L88; active migrated Issues and PRs; report-only #351. Read model outputs as data; trusted publication owns Issue/PR writes. A feedback parent closes only after independently reviewed goal evidence, never from a model success assertion or child closure alone.

## Dependencies
Blocked by #399: the Issue queue and this acceptance specification must be on main first.

## Queue
Key: feedback-goals
Priority: 0
Mode: implement
Provider: codex

## Feedback
Parent goal: #394. The user should not have to label, decompose or repeatedly unblock their own feedback. Existing Issues #355, #356, #369, #389 and #391 provide real intake cases; do not duplicate work already represented by #349/#392/#393.

evidence.remaining: Passing tests prove the controller's logic only. Still unobserved: reconcile dispatching #394 from an ordinary collaborator Issue with no user label, recorded on GitHub.

evidence.command: gh api repos/saadshahd/roundup/issues/394/sub_issues; gh issue list --label loop:work --state open; git ls-remote origin 'refs/heads/loop-row/*' 'refs/heads/loop-feedback/*'
evidence.output: #394 children: #399 (closed), #401 (open, ready-for-agent, Key feedback-goals, live Claim loop-row/feedback-goals). #401 already owns L90 and its unmet observer: one complete real feedback cycle. PR #427 (merged) implemented L90's runtime with 'Refs #401' and left #401 open. No other open work Issue owns L90, so this plan reuses #401 unchanged.
evidence.remaining: Exact-head review of this planning PR, and evidence that its publication created no duplicate owner.

evidence.output: L90 Observer: 'Execute one complete real feedback cycle through GitHub Issues and its independent review gates; record the source revision, plan, native children, delivery and verification evidence. Until that observer passes, feedback automation remains incomplete.'
evidence.remaining: No real cycle has completed yet. This #394 cycle (revision c30f3686…) is the first. Goals 3–7 need this plan reviewed and published, #401's acceptance demonstrated, and a fresh verify run.
